The actor recorded in the ledger for acts made through these tools. Default webmcp.

Register <prefix>read and <prefix>wait when the surface has page content. Default true.

modelContext?

The WebMCP object to register with. Default: document.modelContext when it has registerTool. Pass null to disable, or an object of your own (tests, a polyfill).

requestApproval?
optional requestApproval?: (request) => MaybePromise<boolean | WebMcpApprovalDecision>;

Ask the person before a high-risk action, an action that declares confirm, or a control whose surface state says approval_required. This is trusted application UI: it must show the exact request and resolve only from the person's interaction. Never implement it with anything an agent can invoke. Without it, approval-sensitive calls are refused.

What to do with a control that is unavailable right now: describe (default) registers its tool with the reason in the description, so the agent can tell the user why; omit leaves it out until it becomes available.

Functions

exposeWebMcp()

function exposeWebMcp(surface, options?): WebMcpHandle;

Register the surface's controls and observation as WebMCP tools on this page, plus page read and wait tools when this is an auto surface, and keep them in step with the surface: every change subscribe reports re-derives the set and re-registers only tools whose name, description, schema, or hints changed.

Feature-detected: without a WebMCP object nothing is registered and the handle says supported: false with the reason. Browser-driving agents can still use surface.expose(), and server-side agents the AXE bridge (@summationai/axe-surface/axe) and @summationai/axe-mcp.

Parameters

surface

Surface

options?

WebMcpOptions = {}

Returns
